sentences.text: Panzhousaurus was a reptile belonging to the family Pachypleurosauridae, a group of marine reptiles.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — measures 36 cm long, with an estimated total body length of less than 50 cm, and features a shortened, rounded snout.
Its skeleton includes a neck with 24 cervical vertebrae and an upper back containing 20 dorsal vertebrae.
The arm bones show a straight ulna with a concave posterior margin and a wrist possessing four distally located carpal bones.
The genus was originally described by Jiang and colleagues in 2019, with the type species named Panzhousaurus rotundirostris.
In 2026, Tan, Xu, and Shang described a new specimen from the Middle Triassic Guanling Formation in China.
Taxonomically, Panzhousaurus belongs to the parent group Pachypleurosauridae and is classified within that same family.
Fossils of this animal date to the Middle Triassic period.
